subject: Capacity zoning add-on for CoreHealth private cluster renewal
messages:
From: Timothy Lang <t.lang@corehealth.io>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@corehealth.io
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + new isolation cluster request

Hi Dev,

Our renewal is coming up in July and the architecture team has asked us to formalize an isolation plan for a separate private environment. Primary asks:
- Add a dedicated VPC with two additional inference clusters (for Prod/DR)
- Enforced tenant isolation for PHI workflows (network zoning + KMS segregation)
- Preserve existing traffic routing during cutover (minimal downtime)

Budgeting-wise we were hoping to roll this into the renewal amendment rather than a separate procurement. Can you share a rough MAP (mutual action plan) and an estimate for committed capacity and term options (1 yr vs 3 yr)? Also please confirm whether Redwood can support customer-managed KMS keys for the new environment.

Thanks,
Tim
Timothy Lang
Director, IT Architecture
CoreHealth Inc

---
Attachment: requirements-draft-corehealth.docx (type: docx)

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Lang <t.lang@corehealth.io>
Cc: procurement@corehealth.io
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + new isolation cluster request

Tim — thanks for the clear asks. We can absolutely fold the additional private VPC and two clusters into an amendment at renewal. High-level answers up front:
- We support customer-managed KMS (via our Private deployment integration).
- Two clusters for Prod/DR with dedicated tenancy is a common pattern; we typically size the clusters by steady RPS and peak concurrent sessions.
- We can propose 1-year and 3-year committed-capacity pricing, with deeper discounts on a 3-year term.

I'll send an initial MAP and capacity estimate by EOD Tuesday. To make the estimate accurate, could you confirm:
1) concurrent sessions at peak and average daily tokens per session (approx)
2) desired RTO for failover between clusters
3) whether you require air-gapped onboarding or VPC peering only

Looping in our solutions lead for capacity sizing and the contracts lead for amendment flow.

Best,
Dev Patel
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Renewal + new isolation cluster request — CoreHealth (need sizing + security checklist)

Marissa / Soojin — forwarding CoreHealth's request. TL;DR: they want a separate private VPC with two clusters (Prod + DR), tenant/KMS isolation for PHI, and to fold the work into their renewal amendment.

Ask:
- Marissa: can you draft a MAP that includes milestones (SOW sign, infra build, ingress cutover, validation window) and suggest realistic lead times? Assume we need 6 weeks for provisioning + 2 weeks validation if they approve the design quickly.
- Soojin: please confirm the security checklist items we'd need to include (customer-managed KMS, audit logs retention, SOC 2 mappings, network zoning guidance). Also advise whether the onboarding should be labeled "airgapped" or "VPC-peering + restricted egress" based on their note about minimal downtime. My read: they want KMS segregation but not necessarily physical airgap.

I've attached the draft MAP and a network diagram stub for you to edit. We should aim to have a client-facing MAP and capacity estimate by Wednesday so we can move to procurement.

Thanks,
Dev

Tim — appreciate the clarity on scope. Attached is a proposed Mutual Action Plan and two capacity/term options. Summary below: 

Summary proposal
- Provisioning: dedicated Private VPC + two clusters (primary + DR). Estimated provisioning lead time: 6 weeks from SOW signature.
- Security: customer-managed KMS supported; we will provide an integration runbook and include audit-log export to your SIEM.
- Cutover approach: staged traffic shift with blue/green validation; expected downtime < 30 minutes for control-plane cutover, zero data-plane disruption anticipated.
- Pricing options: 1-year committed capacity ($X/month) or 3-year committed capacity with 18% discount (detailed numbers in MAP attachment).

Requested items from CoreHealth to finalize estimate
1) Average session token count (or sample traces)
2) Desired RTO for the DR cluster
3) Preferred KMS provider and key ARN (if you want us to pre-configure)

Next steps
- If procurement confirms we can proceed via amendment, we will issue a draft SOW and amendment (legal).
- I'll schedule a 30-minute technical review next week with our Solutions team (Marissa) and Security (Soojin) to finalize the checklist and acceptance criteria.

If that works, let me know a few slots for next week and we'll lock the calendar.

Best regards,
Dev Patel
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
